findings.claim: Rule (b) accepts a near-match anchor with diacritics removed, which contract §5 forbids ('does not accept ... a near match as an anchor') and the installed DEVAI resolver rejects. markdownSlugs() adds a second slug for each heading after NFD normalization and mark stripping. DEVAI 1.5.6 anchor-resolver (release-host.js:172322-172345) builds only slugify(heading) and then tests anchor or slugify(anchor). For the heading '## Decisão', DEVAI's slug is 'deciso', so DEVAI rejects the anchor 'decisao'. This gate accepts it. The gate is therefore more permissive than both the contract and `devai check --only invariants`. `pnpm check` runs only this gate, so it would pass an anchor that DEVAI fails.
findings.fix: Inspector first: in tools/law/tests/verify.test.mjs, change the positive fixture anchor for '## Decisão' to the DEVAI-resolvable form. Add a negative case asserting that 'decisao' against '## Decisão' produces AUTHORITY_ANCHOR_UNRESOLVED. Engineer then: delete the NFD variant so heading slugs equal DEVAI extractHeadingSlugs exactly, keeping only the DEVAI-equivalent anchor||slugify(anchor) test. Architect records in CTG-0001 §5 that anchor matching is defined as DEVAI anchorExists equivalence.

findings.claim: The rule (b) positive test requires the gate to accept anchor 'decisao' for heading '## Decisão' (line 193). This is the Inspector locking in the near-match leniency described above. It is a test encoding a weaker rule than the contract, not a neutral fixture.
findings.fix: Replace it with an anchor that the DEVAI resolver accepts, and add the negative diacritic-stripped case, as part of the fix above. Engineer changes follow the test change.

findings.claim: OD resolution is hard-coded to the '## R-0019 — law-corpus' section. Contract §5's resolution table says an OD resolves to 'a table row in docs/meta/knowledge-base/open-decisions-rait.md', without limiting it to one section. Any valid canonical OD cited in provenance from another section (for example OD-R18-001 at open-decisions-rait.md:368) is reported as REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED. This permanent gate will then fail valid CTG-0002 and later provenance, and pressure authors to duplicate ODs into R-0019. No test covers an OD registered outside the R-0019 section.
findings.fix: Inspector: add a positive test with an OD row in another '## ...' section and keep the negative test for an unregistered OD. Engineer: resolve an OD ID against the first cell of any table row in the registry file. C-01-05's specific requirement that OD-R19-* resolve in the R-0019 section is then covered by the existing positive test.
